instrument_name: HRS 387-2 Minimum wages (Wayback copy of capitol.hawaii.gov, snapshot 2025-05)
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum wage 16.00 USD/h from 2026-01-01; 18.00 USD/h from 2028-01-01 (L 2022 c 114). Tip credit: tipped employee may be paid 1.25 USD/h below minimum (from 2024-01-01), 1.50 USD/h below from 2028-01-01, only if employer wage + tips >= minimum wage + 7.00 USD

instrument_name: DLIR Wage Standards Division - Minimum Wage and Overtime page
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum wage 16.00 USD/h from 2026-01-01, 18.00 from 2028-01-01 (matches HRS 387-2). Overtime after 40 h/workweek (HRS 387-3); on state/county public works (HRS ch.104) overtime after 8 h/day and all hours on Sat, Sun and state holidays (HRS 104-2(c))

instrument_name: HRS 387-1 Definitions (employee exclusions) and 387-3 Maximum hours (Wayback copies, snapshot 2025-05)
figure_or_rule_carried: State wage-hour law excludes employees at guaranteed compensation of 4,000 USD or more a month (L 2024 c 73); agriculture with <20 employees; casual domestic service; companionship. Tipped employee = customarily >20 USD/month tips. Overtime 1.5x after 40 h/workweek; regular rate for salaried: weekly/40, biweekly/2/40, semimonthly x24/52/40, monthly x12/52/40; seasonal agricultural processing exemption 20 weeks (OT after 48); split shifts within 14 consecutive hours

instrument_name: DOTAX Withholding Tax - For Employers page (filing, deposit, e-file methods)
article_or_section: Overview; FAQs Return Filing and Payments
figure_or_rule_carried: Booklet A (Rev. 2025, posted 12/1/2025) is still the current rate source at 2026-11-02 (no 2027 booklet posted). HW-14 quarterly, due Apr 15/Jul 15/Oct 15/Jan 15; deposits semi-weekly (>40,000 liability), monthly (5,000-40,000, by 15th of next month), quarterly (<5,000). W-2/HW-2 to employee and DOTAX by 31 January (TA 2021-08); HW-30 only for paper W-2 submissions; HW-3 not required since TY2020 (one FAQ still says 'by February 28 using Form HW-3' - stale FAQ text, contradicts the page body and Booklet A s.2). instrument_name: DOTAX Tax Announcement No. 2025-05 Mandatory electronic filing of Forms W-2 and HW-2 for employers filing 10 or more
figure_or_rule_carried: From 2026-01-01 W-2/HW-2 must be e-filed with DOTAX if the employer files 10 or more in the calendar year, or annual withholding liability > 40,000 (TA 2019-11). Penalty up to 25 per form not e-filed, max 50 per employee (HRS 235-63). Authority HRS 231-9.9(a), conforming to Treas. Reg. 301.6011-2

instrument_name: HRS 388-2 Semimonthly payday; method of payment (Wayback copy, snapshot 2026-09-29)
figure_or_rule_carried: Wages paid at least twice each calendar month on regular paydays designated in advance; monthly only by secret-ballot majority election (valid 2 years) or director permission; earned wages due within 7 days after end of pay period (15 days with director permission). Means: cash, check, direct deposit (voluntary written/e-signature authorization, FDIC-insured, cancellable, no fees, no penalty for refusing, pay statement per 388-7(4)) or other means under 388-5.7 (payroll card, text not read)

instrument_name: HRS 388-3 Employees separated from the payroll before paydays (Wayback copy, snapshot 2025-04)
figure_or_rule_carried: Discharge: wages in full at time of discharge, or not later than the next working day if immediate payment impossible. Resignation: next regular payday (by mail if requested); if employee gave at least one pay period's notice, all wages at time of quitting. Layoff/labor-dispute suspension: next regular payday. Case note (Hawaii Supreme Court 2005, 108 H. 411): unused vacation pay is not 'wages' under 388-1, so no statutory payout of accrued vacation

instrument_name: HRS 388-6 Withholding of wages (Wayback copy, snapshot 2026-01-28)
figure_or_rule_carried: Deductions only when required by federal/state statute or court process, or authorized in writing by the employee; never (even with authorization): fines; shared-till cash shortages; breakage; dishonored checks; losses from workmanship/theft/damage/customer default unless wilful; employer-required medical exams (para (6) ERISA-preempted per case notes)

instrument_name: HRS 383-61 Payment of contributions; wages not included (taxable wage base) (Wayback copy, snapshot 2026-06-14)
figure_or_rule_carried: UI contributions are employer-only and may not be deducted from wages (a). Taxable wage base = average annual wage for the 4 quarters ending 30 June of the preceding year, computed on or before 30 November, rounded to the nearest hundred dollars (b). Successor counts predecessor wages incl. employment under another state's law (e); base never below FUTA base (f). Derivation check: DCD 2026 notice state average annual wage 64,471.82 rounded to nearest 100 = 64,500 = DLIR 2026 UI wage base (Python) - consistent, caliber identity assumed (both DLIR R&S averages)

instrument_name: DLIR UI Contribution Rates Explained (Table 1 history, experience rating, E&T)
article_or_section: Table 1; New Employer Contribution Rate; Tax Base; E&T Assessment; Example for 2026
figure_or_rule_carried: 2026: Schedule C, tax base 64,500, new employer 2.4%, E&T 0.01% (2025: C, 62,000, 2.4%, 0.01%). New-employer rate = rate for reserve ratio .0000. Reserve ratio = reserve balance 31 Dec / average annual taxable payroll of past 3 years; rate notice mailed in March. E&T due from employers with rate > 0% and < schedule maximum, on taxable wages, not creditable against FUTA. Worked example 2026: reserve 10,206.13 / avg payroll 81,666.04 = 0.1250 -> 0.4% (Schedule C). Table 2 (full rate schedules A-H) is not in the page text - minimum rate of Schedule C not transcribed

instrument_name: DLIR UI Handbook for Employers (web edition)
article_or_section: I Contributions: Registration; Quarterly Wage, Contribution and E&T Assessment Report; Taxable wages; Penalties; SIDES
figure_or_rule_carried: Register online (uiclaims.hawaii.gov; paper UC-1 not accepted) - status report within 20 days after hiring. Form UC-B6 quarterly wage/contribution/E&T report due last day of month after quarter (Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31), filed even with no wages, incl. self-financed and 0.00% employers; wage record lists name, SSN, total wages of each covered worker; reported when paid not when earned; online via 'Employer Reporting'. Taxable base: 'Wages paid by an employer to an employee reported to another state during the calendar year may be combined with Hawaii wages' (MULTI-OQ-2: yes for HI); predecessor wages combinable. Penalties: late contributions 10% (min 100) + 2/3% interest per month; late UC-B6 30; late separation report UC-BP-35 10 (5 calendar days). Multiple Worksite Report BLS 3020 for 10+ employees in secondary locations

instrument_name: DLIR UI Excluded Services Not Covered under the Hawaii Employment Security Law (Rev. 1/08)
figure_or_rule_carried: UI excluded: agricultural labor if < 20,000 cash wages each quarter and <= 9 workers in any week / <= 19 weeks (H-2A aliens excluded); domestic service if < 1,000 cash in every quarter of current/preceding year; casual labor < 50/quarter and < 24 days; family employment (parent, spouse, child < 21); federal/other-state government; nonprofit workers < 50/quarter; ordained church members; enrolled students of the school and school-to-work students; student nurses and interns; commission-only insurance, real estate, travel, vacuum-cleaner sales; newspaper carriers < 18; IRC 3508 direct sellers; election workers (IRC 3309(b)(3)(F)); inmates; elective exclusion for two family members each owning >= 50% of a family corporation (irrevocable 5 years). Rev. 1/08 - older than the current law; the web handbook adds Medicaid HCBS caregivers

instrument_name: HRS 392-43 TDI authority to withhold contributions; maximum weekly wage base (Wayback copy, snapshot 2025-02)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer may withhold from each employee one-half of the TDI cost, not more than 0.5% of weekly wages; employer bears the balance; withholding period = employee pay period. Weekly wages exclude (1) wages of an employee who in the preceding 52 weeks has not earned at least 400 and had 14 weeks of 20+ hours, and (2) remuneration above (state average annual wage per 383-61(b) / 52) x 1.21, published by the director before 1 January. Over-withholding refundable

instrument_name: DLIR DCD 2026 Maximum Weekly Wage Base and Maximum Weekly Benefit Amount (TDI, WC, PHC) - re-read of the registered copy
figure_or_rule_carried: TDI max weekly wage base 1,500.21 = 64,471.82/52 x 1.21 (re-derived in Python: 1,500.21); max weekly employee deduction 7.50 (0.5%); TDI max weekly benefit 871.00. PHC: regular employee = 20+ h/week and monthly wage >= 86.67 x state minimum wage = minimum monthly wage 1,387.00 (86.67 x 16.00 = 1,386.72, shown rounded up to 1,387.00); employee PHC share <= half the premium and <= 1.5% of wages, employer liable for the rest. Closes the 86.67x gap noted on US-HIP7-003

instrument_name: HRS 393-3 Prepaid Health Care Act definitions (employer, employment) (Wayback copy, snapshot 2025-02)
figure_or_rule_carried: PHC 'employer' = any organization with one or more regular employees; excludes the State and its subdivisions, the US government, other states and qualifying foreign governments. Employment = service for wages under any contract of hire, except 393-4/393-5 exclusions (not read)

instrument_name: HRS 388-5.7 Payment of wages by pay cards (Wayback copy, snapshot 2026-01-10)
figure_or_rule_carried: Pay card only with employee choice among direct deposit, check or pay card; never mandatory or a condition of hire; voluntary written/e-signature authorization after plain-language disclosure (10-point font: options, fee schedule, third-party fees, free services); switch to another method within two pay periods of written request; free: issuance, loading, 3 withdrawals per pay period (one for full net wages at an insured institution), 24/7 balance access, 60-day history, no overdraft fees, no balance-based fees, one free replacement per year

instrument_name: HRS 398-3 Family leave requirement (Hawaii Family Leave Law) (Wayback copy, snapshot 2025-06)
figure_or_rule_carried: Four weeks of family leave per calendar year for birth/adoption or to care for child, spouse, reciprocal beneficiary, sibling, grandchild or parent with a serious health condition; intermittent allowed; not cumulative; unpaid (exempt employee may be required to make up leave in same pay period). Employer-size threshold in 398-1 (100+ employees, lead) not read

instrument_name: HRS 652-1 Garnishee process; garnishee fund (wage garnishment limits) (Wayback copy, snapshot 2026-09-23)
figure_or_rule_carried: Creditor garnishment (before or after judgment) of wages remaining after deductions required by law: 5% of the first 100 USD per month, 10% of the next 100 USD per month, 20% of all sums above 200 USD per month, or the weekly equivalent. Summons amount <= 120% of the claim. Hawaii's cap is stricter than CCPA 25% for most earners (apply the lower)

instrument_name: HRS 104-3 Payrolls and payroll records (public works certified payroll) (Wayback copy, snapshot 2025-02)
figure_or_rule_carried: Public-works contracts (ch.104, over 2,000 per US-HI-P5-2-002): certified copy of all payrolls plus a certified fringe-benefit reporting form (health/welfare, pension/annuity, vacation, training, other) submitted WEEKLY to the contracting agency; general contractor submits subcontractors' payrolls; site payroll records (name, classification, rate, fringe form, daily and weekly hours, deductions, wages paid) kept 3 years; produced within 10 days of written request

instrument_name: CSEA State Directory of New Hires Questions and Answers (FLO100) and W-4 File Format for Employers (FLO101)
authority: Hawaii Department of the Attorney General, Child Support Enforcement Agency
figure_or_rule_carried: All Hawaii employers (incl. government, nonprofits, any size) report new hires (never employed, or separated >= 60 consecutive days) to CSEA no later than 20 days after the employee's first day of work. Data: employee name, address, SSN, first day services performed, employer name, address, FEIN (state of hire, state EIN, DOB optional). Penalty 25 late; 500 for conspiracy. Separations not reported. Channels: copy of federal W-4 by fax/mail, or SFTP text file in the FLO101 fixed-width layout (H4 header with FEIN, CCYYMMDD date stamp, batch no.; W4 data records; total record; CR LF); internet transmission not available

instrument_name: CSEA Hawaii Employer's Guide - Income Withholding for Child Support Obligations (FEN125, 04/2003)
authority: Hawaii Department of the Attorney General, Child Support Enforcement Agency
figure_or_rule_carried: Support order has priority over garnishment, attachment, execution and other withholding orders. Start no later than the first pay period occurring within 7 business days after the order is mailed; remit to CSEA (or designated payee) within 5 working days after payday; employer may collect a 2 USD administrative fee per payment, from income not from support; total limited by CCPA (50%/60%, +5% if 12+ weeks arrears); combined check with per-employee listing allowed; on termination notify last known address and new employer. Refusal to hire or discharge because of support = misdemeanor. Guide dated 2003 - statutory cross-check of 576E-16 not done this pass

instrument_name: DLIR WSD FAQ on the Hawaii Family Leave Law (HRS ch.398)
figure_or_rule_carried: HFLL covers employers with 100+ employees in Hawaii for each working day in 20+ calendar weeks of current or preceding year (count excludes mainland/international staff); eligible after 6 consecutive months of service (no hours test). Leave unpaid unless employee substitutes accrued paid leave; employer that provides sick leave must allow up to 10 days of accrued and available sick leave (PTO counts) for family leave purposes; HFLL does not require any sick leave plan (Q4) - corroborates absence of a general paid-sick-leave mandate in Hawaii

instrument_name: DLIR Wage Standards Division home page and Guidelines index (laws administered)
article_or_section: Home page programme list; Guidelines page
figure_or_rule_carried: WSD administers ch.387 (minimum wage/overtime), ch.388 (payment of wages: at least twice a month, within 7 days of period end), ch.390 (child labor permits to age 18), ch.104 (prevailing wage; WSD 2017-01 certified payroll memo; WSD 2026-01 of 2026-05-21 on truck drivers), ch.398 (family leave), unlawful termination. No private-sector paid sick leave law appears among the laws administered (negative finding, supported by HFLL FAQ Q4)

instrument_name: DLIR WSD Child Labor page (work permits, hours of 14-15 year olds)
article_or_section: Certificate of Employment; Certificate of Age; Theatrical
figure_or_rule_carried: Work permit required for minors until 18. Ages 14-15: Certificate of Employment (CL-1, per employer and occupation) before work starts; max 3 h school day / 8 h non-school day, 18 h school week / 40 h non-school week, 7am-7pm (6am-9pm before non-school days), 6 consecutive days, 30-min break after 5 h. Ages 16-17: Certificate of Age (eCL-3, online) valid to 18; employer verifies, records the certificate number, returns it. Under 14 only theatrical (HAR 12-25-22..24). Stricter of state/federal applies

instrument_name: Form HW-4 Employee's Withholding Allowance and Status Certificate (Rev. 2022) with instructions
figure_or_rule_carried: Current HW-4 edition is Rev. 2022 (in 'forms/current' at 2026-11-02). Marital status: Single / Married / Married but withhold at higher Single rate / Certified Disabled Person (not subject to withholding) / Nonresident Military Spouse (not subject to withholding). Line 4 total allowances (worksheet), line 5 additional amount per pay period. Hawaii law does NOT allow 'exempt' status. HoH withheld as Single but may claim an extra allowance. New certificate within 10 days on divorce/separation, spouse claiming own allowance, dependent ceasing to qualify; by 1 December on death of spouse/dependent. No HW-4 = Single, zero allowances. Civil-union partners treated as married

instrument_name: HRS 487J-2 Social security number protection (Wayback copy, snapshot 2025-06)
figure_or_rule_carried: Businesses may not publicly display a full SSN, print it on access cards, require its transmission over an unsecured/unencrypted internet connection, use it alone as a website login, or print a full SSN on mailed materials - except employer-to-employee communications or documents required by law; permitted mailed SSNs never visible on a postcard or through the envelope. No Hawaii rule requires SSN truncation on the pay statement; HRS 387-6(c) does not list the SSN among the 14 pay-statement items (US-HI-P5-2-001)

figure_or_rule_carried: Act 24 SLH 2026 (SB 3125 CD2), in force: amends the TY2027 and TY2029 income-tax schedules - 2nd bracket rate 3.2% -> 2.5%, 3rd bracket 5.5% -> 5%, new 13% top bracket for taxable income over 500,000 (single), 750,000 (HoH), 1,000,000 (joint); level = assessment, and withholding from 2027-01-01 once DOTAX issues the 2027 Booklet A tables (not yet published).
